claims.text: UK AISI and the US Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI) jointly published a preliminary assessment on 23 July 2026 finding Kimi K3 performs significantly below the most recent frontier cyber-capable closed models
claims.reasoning: Confirmed verbatim against the AISI/CAISI primary blog post; corroborated by SCMP's independent write-up with matching framing.

claims.text: On ExploitBench, Kimi K3 scored 32% versus GLM-5.2's 24%, but achieved arbitrary code execution on none of 41 test samples, while leading US frontier models averaged arbitrary code execution on 20 of 41
claims.reasoning: A secondary-source search initially surfaced an unconfirmed framing (an overall '32.2% vs 76.2%' comparison). Re-fetched the AISI primary text directly to check attribution: the 32%/24% figure is specifically ExploitBench's score comparing Kimi K3 to GLM-5.2, quoted verbatim from the primary post ('Kimi K3 achieves a score of 32%, whereas GLM-5.2 achieves a score of 24%'); the primary post does not give a single overall percentage score comparable to a US-frontier average, and explicitly states Kimi K3's overall estimate has a wider confidence interval since it rests on one benchmark. The unconfirmed '76.2%' framing was excluded from the published claim set.

claims.text: On 'The Last Ones,' a 32-step simulated corporate-network attack, Kimi K3 reached step 17 of the path on average versus 28.5 for leading US frontier models, and completed the full attack path in 1 of 10 attempts
claims.reasoning: Confirmed against AISI primary text; matching figures independently reported by SCMP.

claims.text: Kimi K3's safeguards allowed the model to assist with agentic cyber exploit development during the evaluation rather than refusing, unlike more restricted alternatives
claims.reasoning: Confirmed verbatim against AISI primary text.

notes: AISI/CAISI joint post is Tier-0 (AISI already registered; CAISI is the US NIST-housed counterpart, treated as the same tier as the joint publication's primary venue). SCMP is Tier-2 independent reporting, not a repost of the primary text. Research-finding claim type, confirmed against the institutes' own primary evaluation; article notes it is a preliminary blog post, not a peer-reviewed or final capability determination.
